correctness.rationale: For each N the Hoeffding grid of O(N^4) frequencies and bounded derivative constructs one point per unit/N interval whose exponential sum approximates Lebesgue integral uniformly by O(sqrt(log N/N)). Smoothing with uniform bumps r_N=epsilon N^{-1-b} supplies decay alpha=1/[2(1+b)] modulo logarithm and any rho<alpha. H1 atoms probe theta log_2 N <= k <= b log_2 N disjoint positive level sets, where center gaps exclude upstream bumps and downstream bumps cannot reach the negative atom lobe. Superlacunary N_m=2^{q^{2m}} with masses (q-1)q^{-m} preserves uniform rho-decay while earlier components are pointwise negligible and later components controlled by L1 tail and Chebyshev, giving unbounded weak norms ~q^{m+1}. Strict parameter ranges b in (0,1/2), theta in (0,b) and rho<1/(2(1+b)) verified by fresh calculations; analytic estimates, not numerical approximation, prove infinity.
residual_risks: Constants require choosing the mixture gap q sufficiently large depending on b,theta; the measures depend on rho.
No rho=1/2 or higher bound is claimed, and existence of centers is probabilistic.
